name: Georgian Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Makharoblidze, Tamar 2012, Georgian Sign Language grammar sketch (336 pp., Glottolog MED) — not found online; sign language, spoken-word stress likely N/A

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x page for geor1254 (https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/geor1254) and English Wikipedia 'Georgian Sign Language'
sources.note: Glottolog lists only subclassification references (Russian SL family), no descriptive refs; Wikipedia has no grammar/phonology content.

sources.citation: Makharoblidze, Tamar. 2024. Affixes of nouns in Georgian Sign Language (GESL). International Journal of Multilingual Education. doi:10.22333/ijme.2024.8993
sources.note: Nothing on stress; only that in sign languages 'signs change their phonological features to display grammatical categories' and GESL has mixed sequential/simultaneous morphology.

sources.citation: Makharoblidze, Tamar. 2024. On case system in Georgian Sign Language. Ena da kultura. doi:10.52340/lac.2024.09.30; 2023 On numerals in GESL (doi:10.52340/idw.2023.33); 2023 Expressive forms of quality in GESL (doi:10.52340/lac.2023.30.04); 2021 On negation in GESL (doi:10.52340/idw.2021.508); 2014 Polypersonal verbal categories in GESL (ms., Ilia SU eprints 3051)
sources.note: None of these five morphosyntax papers mentions stress, prosody, accent or intonation (grep of full text, zero hits).

sources.citation: Makharoblidze, Tamar. 2023. Iconicity in Georgian Sign Language (GESL). Ena da kultura. doi:10.52340/lac.2023.07
sources.note: No mention of stress/prosody/accent (the only 'phonological' hit is a bibliography entry).

sources.citation: Nanitashvili, Ekaterine. 2023. The history of Georgian Sign Language (GESL) linguistics. Ena da kultura (enadakultura). doi:10.52340/lac.2023.09 (5 pp., Georgian)
sources.note: Nothing; surveys GESL research (2015 dictionary 4000 entries, 2016 dactyl alphabet, 2018/2015 SLL papers, 2019 verb-morphology monograph, 2022 overview article). No phonology/prosody work listed.

sources.citation: Pfau, Roland, Tamar Makharoblidze & Hedde Zeijlstra. 2022. Negation and negative concord in Georgian Sign Language. Frontiers in Psychology 13:734845. doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2022.734845
sources.note: Nothing on stress/prosodic prominence in GESL; 'prosodic break' mentioned only for a Jordanian SL example. Background (p. 2): 'In 2012, an overview of the language, including sociolinguistic information and a sketch of its grammar, has been published (Makharoblidze, 2012), followed by the publication of a GESL-Georgian dictionary with 4,000 entries (Makharoblidze, 2015a)'. Ref list gives the 2012 book as Kartuli jest'uri ena, Tbilisi: Ministry of Education and Science, USAID, Save the Children International.

sources.citation: Makharoblidze, Tamar & Roland Pfau. 2018. A negation-tense interaction in Georgian Sign Language. Sign Language & Linguistics 21(1):135-149. doi:10.1075/sll.00013.mak
sources.note: No mention of stress, prosody, accent or phonology.

sources.citation: Makharoblidze, Tamar. 2017. On modality in Georgian Sign Language (GESL). Languages of the Caucasus 2(1). doi:10.5070/L921046890
sources.note: Nothing on stress; only that non-manual components 'play an important role in modal constructions across SLs, just like the intonation that is very relevant for certain modal constructions in many spoken languages'.

sources.citation: Makharoblidze, Tamar. 2016. Kartuli daktiluri anbani [The Georgian dactyl alphabet] (summary), Kavkasiologiuri dziebani 8; Makharoblidze & Mirianashvili 2016, GESL vocabulary and innovation technologies, Proc. XVII EURALEX
Makharoblidze, Tamar. 2016. Lingvisturi ts'erilebi III [Linguistic Letters III]. Tbilisi: Ilia State University. 492 pp. (collected papers incl. GESL lexicon, tense, version, dictionary concept)
sources.note: The only 'stress/intonation' hits (p. ~407 area and a dictionary entry for 'segment') concern spoken Georgian speech therapy and terminology, not GESL. GESL chapters are lexical/morphological; nothing on sign prosody.

sources.citation: Georgian Sign Language Dictionary (online), Ilia State University, https://gesl.iliauni.edu.ge/ (online version of Makharoblidze 2015, 4000 entries)
sources.note: Lexicon with videos and the dactyl alphabet only; no grammar or phonology pages.

sources.citation: Makharoblidze, Tamar. 2015. Indirect object markers in Georgian Sign Language. Sign Language & Linguistics 18(2):238-250. doi:10.1075/sll.18.2.03mak
sources.note: Nothing on stress; one remark that 'phonological erosion is a typical characteristic of grammaticalization'.
